source: Wholesale Price Index (WPI), Office of the Economic Adviser via https://data.gov.in/ (OGD)
note: SEED pack. `value` is the latest WPI YoY inflation (an input-cost proxy); refresh from data.gov.in with scripts/refresh_macro.py --kind inputcost before relying on the magnitude. This overlay has direction=-1: higher WPI is a HEADWIND for input-consuming sectors (positive sensitivity) but a TAILWIND for commodity producers (negative sensitivity — e.g. Metals). `neutral` is the benign-inflation baseline mapping to a zero nudge. `sector_sensitivity` (signed; NSE-Industry + yfinance) is a maintained crosswalk never touched by a fetch. tailwind = clamp((-1)*((value-neutral)/INPUTCOST_SCALE) * sensitivity, -1, 1). Not investment advice.
